data.reasoning: The package is a standard Go application with a pinned source (v1.0.2 tag from official GitHub repository), verified SHA-256 checksum, and conventional build/install procedures. No malicious code, suspicious network requests, or injection patterns were found. The inconclusive verdict from qwen3-235b was due to an API error (HTTP 400) when reviewing .SRCINFO, not a security concern. Two models independently confirmed the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen3-235b model, which failed to review .SRCINFO due to an HTTP 400 API error. This resulted in an inconclusive verdict for that file, which propagated to an overall inconclusive result. The deepseek-v4-flash model successfully reviewed both files and found them safe. The openrouter/free report (advisory: true) also found the package safe but does not count as a vote. There is no actual security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to review .SRCINFO due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), resulting in incomplete coverage
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should not result in inconclusive verdicts for the entire package when other files were successfully reviewed
The audit tool should implement retry logic for transient API errors or provide clearer error messages distinguishing tool failures from security concerns
When a file review fails due to a tool error, the verdict should be based on successfully reviewed files with explicit notation of the coverage gap, rather than defaulting to inconclusive
